title: Granny cluster
subtitle: Three trebles into a chain space — the granny square's core unit
excerpt: The granny cluster is three trebles worked consecutively into the same chain space, with the tops sitting side by side. It is the exact construction at the heart of every granny square and hundreds of motifs descended from it.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volumes 1 and 2 (Internet Archive). Granny square construction and traditional British motif patterns. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), motif crochet chapter.
heroPrompt: Close-up of a granny square showing the three-treble clusters at each side and the ch-2 corner spaces, cream and grey DK cotton, natural background.

glossaryTerms.definition: Three trebles worked consecutively into the same chain space. The standard unit of the granny square pattern, worked in groups with chain spaces between each cluster.

content.text: is 3tr into a chain space: three complete trebles, all worked into the same gap rather than into a stitch. Every granny square uses this as its repeating unit. The clusters sit separated by ch-1 spaces along each side and ch-2 spaces at each corner.
Identify the chain space (the gap formed by chains in the previous round). Insert the hook under the chain, not into any single loop of the chain.
Work 3 complete trebles into that chain space.
The three trebles sit side by side, all emerging from the same chain space below.
Magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr).
Work 2 more tr into the ring (3-tr cluster, with the ch-3 standing as the first tr). Ch 2.
*3tr into the ring, ch 2; repeat from * 2 more times (4 clusters + 4 ch-2 corner spaces).
Sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. Pull the magic ring tail to close the centre.
Sl st across to the ch-2 corner space. Ch 3, 2tr into the corner space, ch 2, 3tr into the same corner space (corner cluster pair made).
Ch 1, *work corner (3tr, ch 2, 3tr) into each ch-2 corner space, ch 1 between corners; repeat from * to end.
Sl st to top of beg ch-3. (4 corners + 4 sides, 8 clusters total.)

items.symptom: The granny square cups or bowls instead of lying flat
items.cause: The tension is too tight, pulling the rounds inward.
items.fix: Relax the yarn tension. Granny squares need a slightly looser hand than flat fabric — the chain spaces need room to open.

items.symptom: The corners are loose and hole-y
items.cause: The ch-2 corner chains were worked too loosely.
items.fix: Work the corner chains snugly. Two chains at the corner is the standard — do not add a third.

items.symptom: The join at the end of a round is visible as a step
items.cause: The sl st join sits slightly higher or lower than the surrounding clusters.
items.fix: Join into the top of the beginning ch-3 (not into the second chain). Draw the slip stitch firmly so it sits flush with the cluster tops.

content.text: Once the basic two-round granny is solid, add more rounds: each new round adds one cluster per side (two clusters at each corner plus one along each existing side). From there, join-as-you-go is the natural next skill — it uses a slip stitch on the final round of each new square to attach it to its neighbour as you crochet.
